rationale_evidence.anchor: Gītā Chapter 3 \rightarrow rich semantic test case \rightarrow architecture validation
rationale_evidence.statement: States the epistemic status of the exercise: NOT claiming Bhagavad-gita = formal specification of KnowledgeOS, but using Chapter 3's narrative/conceptual structure as a rich semantic test case to ask whether the model can faithfully represent the epistemic situation, reasoning, conflict, guidance and action without losing distinctions; notes the source itself frames Arjuna's problem as conflicting instructions and a request for decisive determination of what is most beneficial.

A 19-row final validation matrix scoring prior theory claims (multidimensional epistemic state, conflict is relational, support≠resolution, question has purpose, understanding≠knowledge, ideal state, structured discrepancy, scalar distance secondary, Zero/Lord/Sārathi abstractions, decision readiness, action, agency, norms, role, authority, lineage, transition system) against Chapter 3 evidence, verdicts ranging 'Strongly validated' to 'Major missing concept' (Norms, Role, Authority) to 'Needs extension' (Action, Agency).

Deepest conclusion: KnowledgeOS was thought to be a Knowledge State model but is actually 'An Epistemic-Normative-Decision-Action System' whose central problem is how an agent moves from imperfect understanding through knowledge, interpretation, norms, discrepancy and guidance to authorized action while preserving epistemic provenance and never confusing knowledge, recommendation and decision. Chapter 3's arc is summarized as Confusion->Question->Clarification->Knowledge->Understanding->Norm->Duty->Guidance->Decision->Action. Recommends freezing Purpose/Role/Duty/NormativeState/Authority/Intention/Agency/ActorState/LearningReadiness/Synthesis/PerceivedConflict/DecisionGap/NormativeGap and revising Q16-19 before proceeding to Q20, since Q20 would otherwise formalize a state model missing normative and agency dimensions.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Source observation \rightarrow semantic concept \rightarrow architectural inference \rightarrow formalization
rationale_evidence.statement: Final self-assessment: grades the previous (S0807) analysis by area (A for Knowledge≠Understanding, A- for normative dimension recognition, down to C+ for 'separation of source vs inference'), diagnosing the main weakness as over-formalization too early — good concepts promoted directly to mathematical dimensions. Prescribes a mandatory four-stage gate: Source observation -> semantic concept -> architectural inference -> formalization, and proposes establishing a four-column Chapter-3 extraction table (Verse -> Source concept -> Architectural concept -> Formal status [axiom/derived invariant/heuristic/analogy]) as the rigorous bridge before revising Questions 16-19, presenting a revised bounded-context pipeline diagram (Context->Actor/Knowledge/World->Understanding->{Norms,Criteria}->Zero->Discrepancy->Lord->Sārathi->Decision->Action->Outcome->World/Knowledge update) as the new baseline.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Chapter 3 is strong conceptual evidence for the architecture's core semantic relationships. It is not a proof of our particular software architecture or mathematical formalization.
rationale_evidence.statement: A ten-row table rates Chapter 3's support as 'Strong' for: Knowledge≠Understanding, Understanding->Action, Role->Duty, Normative knowledge, Authority->Guidance, Guidance≠Action, Action->Outcome->changed situation, Observed action≠semantic meaning, Agent condition affects action/knowledge, and Context-dependence of applicable duty — called the 'semantic skeleton' of the architecture.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Chapter 3 \rightarrow Semantic Principles \rightarrow DDD Model \rightarrow Mathematical Model \rightarrow KnowledgeOS Architecture
rationale_evidence.statement: Introduces a three-layer epistemic classification for how the Gita evidence licenses claims: Layer 1 source-supported semantic principles (Knowledge->Understanding->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome, governed by Role+Norm+Context+Authority — 'strongly supported'); Layer 2 mathematical abstraction (S_t, Δ_t, D_t, S_{t+1}=T(...) — 'motivated but not proven'); Layer 3 KnowledgeOS implementation architecture (bounded contexts, Zero/Lord/Sārathi as components — 'not proven, requires independent validation'). Gives a derivation chain Chapter 3 -> Semantic Principles -> DDD Model -> Mathematical Model -> KnowledgeOS Architecture where each arrow is a derivation step, not a claim the source contains the software architecture. Final confidence ratings: core conceptual architecture and DDD concepts strongly supported/motivated; mathematical modelling well-motivated but needing independent validation; specific equations derived-by-us-not-source-proven; fixed discrepancy vector explicitly 'do not freeze'; concrete component architecture requires separate architectural evidence.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Freeze the theory as defined in this document ... The theory is now complete, defensible, and ready for construction.
rationale_evidence.statement: The document's own closing recommendation is to freeze this theory, create a semantic extraction table for future chapters, formalize transition semantics for the clean state model S=(W,K,U,N,A,C), define an algebra of operations for Z/L/Sa, and proceed directly to implementation -- an unadjudicated self-assessment by the external-research source, not a project governance ruling.

## Rationale
States the epistemic status of the exercise: NOT claiming Bhagavad-gita = formal specification of KnowledgeOS, but using Chapter 3's narrative/conceptual structure as a rich semantic test case to ask whether the model can faithfully represent the epistemic situation, reasoning, conflict, guidance and action without losing distinctions; notes the source itself frames Arjuna's problem as conflicting instructions and a request for decisive determination of what is most beneficial. [S0807] A 19-row final validation matrix scoring prior theory claims (multidimensional epistemic state, conflict is relational, support≠resolution, question has purpose, understanding≠knowledge, ideal state, structured discrepancy, scalar distance secondary, Zero/Lord/Sārathi abstractions, decision readiness, action, agency, norms, role, authority, lineage, transition system) against Chapter 3 evidence, verdicts ranging 'Strongly validated' to 'Major missing concept' (Norms, Role, Authority) to 'Needs extension' (Action, Agency). [S0807] Deepest conclusion: KnowledgeOS was thought to be a Knowledge State model but is actually 'An Epistemic-Normative-Decision-Action System' whose central problem is how an agent moves from imperfect understanding through knowledge, interpretation, norms, discrepancy and guidance to authorized action while preserving epistemic provenance and never confusing knowledge, recommendation and decision. Chapter 3's arc is summarized as Confusion->Question->Clarification->Knowledge->Understanding->Norm->Duty->Guidance->Decision->Action. Recommends freezing Purpose/Role/Duty/NormativeState/Authority/Intention/Agency/ActorState/LearningReadiness/Synthesis/PerceivedConflict/DecisionGap/NormativeGap and revising Q16-19 before proceeding to Q20, since Q20 would otherwise formalize a state model missing normative and agency dimensions. [S0807] Final self-assessment: grades the previous (S0807) analysis by area (A for Knowledge≠Understanding, A- for normative dimension recognition, down to C+ for 'separation of source vs inference'), diagnosing the main weakness as over-formalization too early — good concepts promoted directly to mathematical dimensions. Prescribes a mandatory four-stage gate: Source observation -> semantic concept -> architectural inference -> formalization, and proposes establishing a four-column Chapter-3 extraction table (Verse -> Source concept -> Architectural concept -> Formal status [axiom/derived invariant/heuristic/analogy]) as the rigorous bridge before revising Questions 16-19, presenting a revised bounded-context pipeline diagram (Context->Actor/Knowledge/World->Understanding->{Norms,Criteria}->Zero->Discrepancy->Lord->Sārathi->Decision->Action->Outcome->World/Knowledge update) as the new baseline. [S0808] A ten-row table rates Chapter 3's support as 'Strong' for: Knowledge≠Understanding, Understanding->Action, Role->Duty, Normative knowledge, Authority->Guidance, Guidance≠Action, Action->Outcome->changed situation, Observed action≠semantic meaning, Agent condition affects action/knowledge, and Context-dependence of applicable duty — called the 'semantic skeleton' of the architecture. [S0810] Introduces a three-layer epistemic classification for how the Gita evidence licenses claims: Layer 1 source-supported semantic principles (Knowledge->Understanding->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome, governed by Role+Norm+Context+Authority — 'strongly supported'); Layer 2 mathematical abstraction (S_t, Δ_t, D_t, S_{t+1}=T(...) — 'motivated but not proven'); Layer 3 KnowledgeOS implementation architecture (bounded contexts, Zero/Lord/Sārathi as components — 'not proven, requires independent validation'). Gives a derivation chain Chapter 3 -> Semantic Principles -> DDD Model -> Mathematical Model -> KnowledgeOS Architecture where each arrow is a derivation step, not a claim the source contains the software architecture. Final confidence ratings: core conceptual architecture and DDD concepts strongly supported/motivated; mathematical modelling well-motivated but needing independent validation; specific equations derived-by-us-not-source-proven; fixed discrepancy vector explicitly 'do not freeze'; concrete component architecture requires separate architectural evidence. [S0810] The document's own closing recommendation is to freeze this theory, create a semantic extraction table for future chapters, formalize transition semantics for the clean state model S=(W,K,U,N,A,C), define an algebra of operations for Z/L/Sa, and proceed directly to implementation -- an unadjudicated self-assessment by the external-research source, not a project governance ruling. [S1274]
